artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each positive integer $n$, define
$$a_n \;:=\; \frac{1}{2n(2n+1)\binom{2n}{n}} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} (28k+3)\,\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}\,(-3\cdot 2^{12})^{\,n-1-k},$$
where $\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k} = (4k)!/(k!)^4$ is the multinomial coefficient.

(i) Prove or disprove that $(-1)^{n-1}a_n$ is a positive integer for every integer $n \geq 2$.

(ii) Let $p>3$ be a prime, and let $B_m(x)$ denote the Bernoulli polynomial. Prove or disprove that for every positive integer $a$,
$$p^a \sum_{k=0}^{p^a - 1} \frac{28k+3}{(-3\cdot 2^{12})^k}\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k} \;\equiv\; 3\bigl(p^a + p^{a-1}\bigr) - \tfrac{5}{24}\,p^{2}\,B_{p-2}(\tfrac{1}{?})\;\;\;\;\pmod{p^3}.$$
(Here the right-hand side is intended as $3(p^a)+(p^{a-1})\,\frac{5}{24}\,p^2 B_{p-2}(1)$ as in the original formulation.)

(iii) Prove or disprove that for every prime $p>3$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1} \frac{1}{(-3\cdot 2^{12})^{k}}\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k} \;\equiv\;
\begin{cases}
(-1)^{\lfloor x/6\rfloor}(4x^2-2p) \pmod{p^2}, & \text{if } p\equiv 1 \pmod{12},\ p=x^2+y^2,\ x\equiv 1\!\!\pmod 4,\ 2\mid y,\\[4pt]
-4\!\left(\dfrac{xy}{3}\right)\!xy \pmod{p^2}, & \text{if } p\equiv 5\pmod{12},\ p=x^2+y^2,\ x\equiv 1\!\!\pmod 4,\ 2\mid y,\\[4pt]
0 \pmod{p^2}, & \text{if } p\equiv 3 \pmod 4,
\end{cases}$$
where $\left(\frac{\cdot}{3}\right)$ is the Legendre symbol modulo $3$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search for this specific conjecture (a Ramanujan-type supercongruence involving the multinomial coefficient $\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}$ with weight $(28k+3)/(-3\cdot 2^{12})^k$, integrality of an associated sequence, and a $p$-adic evaluation modulo $p^2$ depending on $p=x^2+y^2$) did not return any published proof or disproof. Z.-W. Sun has many such conjectures and some have been resolved by various authors, but no source consulted confirms the status of this particular one. The current status is therefore unclear.

status_evidence.snippet: Collection of Sun's conjectures on congruences and combinatorial identities, including Ramanujan-type series with multinomial coefficients.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture appears in Sun's collection of open conjectures on congruences; no proof or disproof was located in the search results.
